summary: Three explicit opt-in V4 owned backend entries reuse the existing V4 payer client, borrowed native backend reader and sequential core. A synthetic backend success followed by declared response loss leaves a persisted selected-grant quarantine. Reopened no-dispatch and full-client bindings retain that quarantine; cached backend success is data, never new dispatch/payment/signing/delivery authority. Defaults and V3 entry bodies remain unchanged.

selection.lane: P2 existing-component backend-bound client/runner and persistent original-request custody
selection.retainedCoverage: The preceding owned V3 backend selection executes the V3 payer/backend path and explicitly lacks durable reconstruction of transport uncertainty. The preceding V4 native store, owner, HTTP, sequential runner and fresh-process selection qualify their own finite paths but do not import this backend connection. This packet connects the existing V4 owner to the actual borrowed backend composition; it does not replay or relabel those earlier tests.

implementation.behavior: A private default-false persistentCustody parameter selects the existing V4 owned HTTP client only for the three new entry points. The existing sequential core receives its already-supported V4 ownership DATA label. No second lifecycle, native owner, store acquisition, store-close implementation or recovery algorithm is added.
implementation.noDispatchFactory: openServiceCreditCustodiedSqliteBackendRecoveryClientV4 exposes only existing read/snapshot/close methods. It supplies the existing forbidden transport internally and accepts no caller transport, submission or batch escape hatch.
implementation.explicitSubmissionFactories: The full client requires the existing explicit trusted requestImpl capability. The sequential facade exposes one bounded batch and no single-submit escape hatch.
implementation.preservedFences: The exact-original, selected-grant, reread, busy, unavailable, backend-reader close and actual cached owner-close fences are byte-identical. Cached backend success remains nested and cannot clear custody/submission uncertainty or the persisted marker.
implementation.legacySwitch: All existing V3 entry calls retain their original arguments and the new private flag defaults to false. The selected negative case also refuses the V4 database through the existing V3 entry without changing logical rows, schema or owner epoch. This is not a full V3 regression suite.
implementation.configuration: The existing exact DATA-only field lists remain unchanged; the internal mode is not a public configuration switch. Missing transport, an accessor deadline and a proxy transport are refused without invoking getters/proxy traps.
implementation.ownership: Payer store owned by the existing SQLite client; native backend store remains borrowed and usable after each client close. Fixture alone closes its backend/session.
implementation.close: All three owned store closes return once and release their slots, while cached root close Promises still reject CHILD_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. Database release does not erase UNKNOWN.

scenarios.name: V4 backend runner persists uncertainty after backend commit and stops its queued tail
scenarios.coverage: Refuse three malformed configurations before payer mutation. One explicit V4 runner batch attempts its first original through the actual scoped backend. The backend commits one synthetic success before the declared response is lost. The client persists one quarantine, stops the unattempted tail and releases queued references. Native payer close returns while root close remains UNKNOWN.

scenarios.name: V4 no-dispatch backend reader keeps cached success subordinate to persisted quarantine
scenarios.coverage: Normally reopen the same new V4 payer under a no-dispatch surface. Restore PERSISTED_UNKNOWN without another marker write. Exact-original backend recovery returns CLIENT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED containing CACHED_SUCCESS; all action and delivery flags remain false. No HTTP or backend execution is started, and backend query transactions do not change its logical state.

scenarios.name: V4 full backend client refuses new work while legacy V3 stays schema-separated
scenarios.coverage: Reopen the full V4 client and read the same cached backend data. A different original for the quarantined grant rejects CUSTODY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN before new custody/intent/transport work. Logical original, intent, quarantine, funding and schema data are unchanged apart from the successful V4 opens' owner-epoch increments. The existing V3 entry refuses this V4 file without migration/reset or an epoch increment.

nativeFiles.payerOwnerEpoch: Each of the three successful V4 acquisitions advances the existing owner epoch by one; the V3 refusal advances it by zero. The selected assertions compare these deltas and unchanged logical rows/schema, not process-restart durability.
nativeFiles.payerRows: One exact retained original, one insert-only intent and one quarantine. Funding request/payment headers and revision remain unchanged; the queued and new originals are not retained or executed.
nativeFiles.backend: One actual local synthetic execution succeeds. Its cached assertion stays subordinate to client uncertainty and supplies no delivery/current-authority proof.

limits: Only these three exact-source local component registrations are qualified; this is not a default/full suite or broad backend/store/native qualification.
Synthetic activation, funding, transport and deadline behavior are declared. In-memory synthetic capability cryptography is not a wallet/payment signature or real provider approval.
The same-process normal V4 reopens are not process restart, crash, power-loss or live original-payment recovery proof. Prior fresh-process V4 runner evidence has its own source/path boundary.
No native close failure, post-acquisition composition failure, real socket/TLS backpressure, simultaneous writer or cross-store atomicity guarantee is qualified.
Native APIs, current source components and cooperative same-user filesystem/lease behavior remain trusted premises; hashes/modes are not hostile same-user authentication.
Current funding/context, payer/provider/policy authority, real READY, independent commit/uncertainty, inclusion/receive, delivery, economics and live-pilot acceptance remain separate gates.
Earlier failed loaders/readers and pending-promotion outcomes remain retained; none is silently promoted, retried or counted as a pass.
Hosted CI, active/default/CLI adoption and live payment/signing are not run or enabled. Empty CI lists are not green.
